title: O Light of Light! When Other Lights Are Fading
description: O Light of Light! When Other Lights Are Fading in Tonic Solfa to PERFECT LOVE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Elevens and Tens (11.10.11.10), and this page sets them to PERFECT LOVE; any other Elevens and Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Light of light! when oth-er lights are fa-ding, Then in my soul with heav-enly bright-ness shine; "Let there be light!" the night and fear up-braid-ing, Speak Thou the word and send the Light Di-vine.

lines: O Light of light! when other lights are fading,
Then in my soul with heavenly brightness shine;
"Let there be light!" the night and fear upbraiding,
Speak Thou the word and send the Light Divine.
O Joy of joy! when other joys are sighing,
Sing to my soul and bid its sadness flee;
And when the songs my bitter tears are drying,
Come with Thy gladness, and rejoice with me.
O Love of love! when other loves are dying,
And hearts grow cold, and eyes that lured me frown;
Come to my heart, Thou Love, all hate defying,
Full of all pity to our world come down.
O Bliss of bliss! when earth and all its treasures
Shrink from my grasp, and leave me poor and sad;
May I with Christ fill up my empty measures,
And in His presence reap the hopes I had.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to PERFECT LOVE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
